generate.title: Your pairing code
generate.description:
Home Assistant made this code for you:

## `{code}`

Give it to whatever sends your readings: in the PeekESP Windows app that is **Settings, Pair a device**, and the PeekESP app on your phone asks for it too. Submit to start listening on it. Machines appear once an agent has pushed to this code.

The ESP32 display makes a code of its own. To point it at this one instead, open **Configure** on the integration afterwards: the pairing code page shows the Worker URL and read token for the device's setup page.

The code stays the same while this page is open, so you can copy it first. Treat it like a password: anyone who has it can read your readings.

pairing_code.title: Pairing code
pairing_code.description:
## `{code}`

Enter this in the PeekESP Windows app (**Settings, Pair a device**) or the PeekESP app on your phone.

The ESP32 display makes its own code. To point it at this stream instead, open its setup page (hold the left button) and fill in **Relay**:

- Worker URL: `{worker_url}`
- Read token: `{read_token}`

Treat all of this like a password: anyone who has the code can read your readings. Do not post it in issues or on Discord.

pairing_unknown.title: Pairing code
pairing_unknown.description:
Home Assistant does not know this entry's code. It was typed in, and only a read token derived from it was kept, which cannot be turned back into the code. The code is on the device's screen, or in your agent's settings.

For the ESP32's setup page (**Relay**):

- Worker URL: `{worker_url}`
- Read token: `{read_token}`

If you would rather have a code Home Assistant can show, make a new one. Every agent and display using the current code will need the new one.

rotate_code.title: Make a new pairing code
rotate_code.description:
New code:

## `{code}`

Submitting switches this entry to it. **Every agent, app and display using the old code stops reaching this stream** until you enter the new code in each of them. Nothing changes until you submit.

generate_pairing_code.name: Generate pairing code
generate_pairing_code.description: Makes a fresh random pairing code and returns it. Nothing is saved or changed. Give the code to an agent, then add it with Pair.

get_pairing_code.name: Get pairing code
get_pairing_code.description: Returns the pairing code Home Assistant generated for an entry. Not available for entries whose code was typed in. Administrators only, because the code is a credential.

config_entry_id.name: Entry
config_entry_id.description: Which PeekESP entry. Leave empty if there is only one.

rotate_pairing_code.name: Rotate pairing code
rotate_pairing_code.description: Switches an entry to a new generated code and returns it. Agents, the app and the display using the old code stop reaching this stream until they are given the new one.

config_entry_id.name: Entry
config_entry_id.description: Which PeekESP entry. Leave empty if there is only one.

get_links.name: Get project links
get_links.description: Returns the links to rhshourav on GitHub, the PeekESP repositories and the Discord community, and can show them in a notification.

notify.name: Show in a notification
notify.description: Also post the links as a notification, where they can be clicked.

refresh.name: Refresh now
refresh.description: Polls the relay now instead of waiting for the next poll. Held back to one poll per 10 seconds, as the Refresh now button is.

config_entry_id.name: Entry
config_entry_id.description: Which PeekESP entry. Leave empty to refresh all of them.

set_options.name: Set options
set_options.description: Changes the poll interval and the offline timeout, as the options dialog does. The entry reloads.

config_entry_id.name: Entry
config_entry_id.description: Which PeekESP entry. Leave empty to change all of them.

scan_interval.name: Poll interval
scan_interval.description: Seconds between polls of the relay, 5 to 600.

offline_after.name: Offline after
offline_after.description: Seconds without a push before a machine counts as offline, 10 to 3600.

pair.name: Pair with a code
pair.description: Adds an entry from a pairing code, as the setup dialog does. Dashes and case are ignored. Administrators only.

code.name: Pairing code
code.description: The 10-character code from the device, the agent or Generate pairing code.

relay_base.name: Relay address
relay_base.description: Leave as is unless you deployed your own Worker.

store_code.name: Keep the code
store_code.description: Store the code in Home Assistant so Get pairing code can show it later. Off by default: the code can push readings and send commands, and the read token Home Assistant needs cannot.

add_custom_relay.name: Add custom relay
add_custom_relay.description: Adds an entry from a Worker URL and read token, for a named or private stream. Administrators only.

url.name: Worker URL
url.description: The https:// address of the stream.
